clinical_knowledge.topic: Rotator cuff tendinopathy / subacromial impingement syndrome evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Rotator cuff tendinopathy / subacromial impingement syndrome is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes Evidence-based diagnostic and therapeutic protocol for Rotator Cuff Tendinopathy / Subacromial Impingement Syndrome, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: anterolateral shoulder pain worsening with overhead reaching and sleeping on that side

Key HPI features: 50M painter reports 3 months of aching pain in his right shoulder. Pain worsens when painting ceilings, reaching overhead, or sleeping directly on the right shoulder. Denies any sudden fall or injury.
Objective/Exam findings: Complete vital signs and focused physical examination required. Diagnostic workup tailored for Rotator Cuff Tendinopathy / Subacromial Impingement Syndrome.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Rotator cuff tendinopathy / subacromial impingement syndrome.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Rotator cuff tear without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Progressive symptoms without trauma suggest overuse tendinopathy rather than acute tear.
management_principles: Evidence-based diagnostic and therapeutic protocol for Rotator Cuff Tendinopathy / Subacromial Impingement Syndrome
: Perform Neer and Hawkins impingement tests
Recommend physical therapy for rotator cuff strengthening and scapular stabilization
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

Pain worsens when painting ceilings, reaching overhead, or sleeping directly on the right shoulder. Denies any sudden fall or injury.
reference_soap.objective: Complete vital signs and focused physical examination required. Diagnostic workup tailored for Rotator Cuff Tendinopathy / Subacromial Impingement Syndrome.
reference_soap.assessment: Clinical presentation highly suggestive of Rotator Cuff Tendinopathy / Subacromial Impingement Syndrome.
reference_soap.plan: After focused examination, begin activity modification and physical therapy for rotator-cuff and scapular strengthening. Consider analgesia only after reviewing contraindications; a subacromial corticosteroid injection can be considered after assessment if symptoms persist. Obtain imaging or refer if there is traumatic onset, objective or progressive weakness, marked loss of passive motion, systemic symptoms, or failure of conservative care.

history.answer: My right shoulder has been aching for about three months, and it hurts a lot whenever I lift my arm up.
The pain is on the front and outer side of my right shoulder. None of my other joints hurt.
It started gradually about three months ago and has slowly gotten worse over time.
It is a dull, persistent ache that reaches about a 5 or 6 out of 10 when I use the arm.
No, I haven't noticed any swelling, redness, or warmth in the shoulder.
It feels slightly stiff for about five or ten minutes when I first wake up, but it goes away once I start moving.
Reaching overhead or lifting my arm up makes it worse, while resting my arm at my side helps.
Yes, I often wake up with pain if I roll over and sleep on my right shoulder.
I work as a house painter, so painting ceilings and holding a brush overhead for hours really triggers it.
I can still use my hands for light tasks, but reaching high shelves or putting on a coat has become quite difficult.
No, I haven't had any fever, chills, or sweats.
No, I didn't fall, get hit, or feel any sudden tearing sensation. It just came on over time.
No, my shoulder doesn't catch, lock, click, or feel like it is popping out of place.
No, I've never had shoulder trouble or any joint issues before this.
No, I haven't experienced any unusual fatigue, low fevers, or weight loss.
No skin rashes, mouth ulcers, hair loss, or red, dry eyes.
No, I don't have any morning back stiffness or heel pain.
No recent diarrhea, burning when I urinate, genital discharge, or sore throat.
I don't drink alcohol, I don't eat heavy meat or seafood feasts, and I don't take water pills.
I've never had any injections, aspirations, or surgeries on my shoulder.
I think it might be rotator cuff wear-and-tear or muscle strain from all my years of painting.
I'm worried that I might need surgery to fix my shoulder.
I'm hoping to start physical therapy and see if a cortisone injection might help relieve the pain.
I was diagnosed with high blood pressure about five years ago.
I have never had any surgeries or hospital stays.
I take lisinopril 10 milligrams once a day, and occasionally over-the-counter acetaminophen if the ache is bad.
No, I don't have any known drug allergies.
No, I have never smoked cigarettes.
I don't drink any alcoholic beverages.
I work full-time as an interior painter and live in a house with my wife.
My father had high blood pressure, but no one in my family has rheumatoid arthritis or joint diseases.
I have been in a faithful, monogamous marriage with my wife for twenty years.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 128/82 mmHg, heart rate 72 beats per minute, respiratory rate 14 breaths per minute, temperature 36.8°C, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Alert, comfortable-appearing male resting right arm by side without obvious swelling, deformity, or muscle wasting.

Tenderness over the right greater tuberosity and subacromial space without warmth or effusion, with full passive range of motion, a painful arc during active abduction between 60 and 120 degrees, and positive Neer and Hawkins impingement signs.
Full 5/5 strength on bilateral shoulder abduction, external rotation, and internal rotation, with pain on right resisted empty-can testing but no weakness or drop-arm sign.
Intact light touch sensation over the axillary nerve distribution and upper extremities bilaterally.
Biceps, triceps, and brachioradialis reflexes are 2+ and symmetric bilaterally.
Cervical spine demonstrates full painless active range of motion without midline tenderness or reproduction of shoulder pain on Spurling test.
No rash, psoriatic plaques, tophi, or nail pitting on skin inspection.
